episode_row: deferral abandoned enterable picks; 8/30 DM after cutoff; 10.6-min cached-feed sleeps; health read it healthy

commits.subject: fix(scheduler): fail-closed submission-cutoff guard at the delivery chokepoint
commits.body:
_deliver_and_lock_pick refuses to send at/after first pitch − 5 min for the
earliest committed slot, archives the dead candidate (refused_delivery_*.json,
<date>.json removed so later cycles re-pick), records the refusal on
scheduler state and DMs a CRITICAL. Also stamps DailyPick.delivered_at —
run_time is selection time, and the EOD audit needs the send time.

Two existing test files drove deliveries with a clock hours past their
pick's cutoff (a real clock against a 2026-04-06 pick; a 23:30 harness
default); they now pin the clock inside the window.

commits.subject: feat(scheduler): deadline-aware in-loop fallback
commits.body:
After the fallback refresh the loop now re-syncs lineup confirmations,
re-reads the clock and asks plan_fallback_action whether a window that can
change THIS decision can still finish before this pick's deliver-by time
(cutoff − operator_reserve). A gap-rule block with no such window now
DELIVERS the enterable pick (policy change, approved 2026-08-30; previously
it was abandoned whenever any pending window existed — 8/27, 8/29, 8/30).
A projected PRIMARY still defers (2026-07-06 product choice). Overrun
scheduled checks the refresh already covered are coalesced instead of
re-cascading into the cutoff. Cascade durations are measured
(runs_completed.duration_sec, state.fallback_refreshes) and feed a
self-calibrating budget that also floors the fallback deadline at
cutoff + reserve + budget.

Tests: the 16:10/19:05 deferral test flips to delivery under the new policy
(sibling added for the primary-projected case that still defers); the
incident is replayed with an advancing clock (Kwan delivered at 13:20, the
overdue check never runs) and a second replay proves the chokepoint guard
refuses a cascade that overran the cutoff. run_day tests now fail the live
MLB lookup — game_pks 100/200 are real 1999 games with posted lineups.

commits.subject: perf(pull): do not sleep between cached feeds
commits.body:
pull_feeds slept delay (0.3 s) after every discovered game even when
download_game_feed returned a cached file without a request: 2,112 cached
feeds = ~10.6 min of pure sleep on every intraday prediction cascade
(2026-08-30 late-pick incident). Throttle only between real requests.

commits.subject: perf(predict): refresh season data once per day, not per cascade
commits.body:
_refresh_season_data memoizes a successful pull+rebuild per (season,
yesterday) via data/processed/.refreshed_<season>_through_<yesterday>;
later cascades the same day skip the ~12-min no-op re-pull. The skip also
requires the season parquet to exist so a marker can never hide a missing
file. BTS_REFRESH_ALWAYS=1 forces a refresh. Known limitation: a game from
yesterday that finalizes later today is picked up by tomorrow's first refresh.

commits.subject: fix(scheduler): round-2 adversarial review — 11 findings addressed
commits.body:
Codex (gpt-5.6-sol, repo access) reviewed the patch assuming defects; the
real ones, fixed here:
- F8 naive game_time was read in the HOST timezone (a naive intended-UTC
  17:40 made the cutoff four hours late under TZ=America/New_York) — naive
  values are now assumed UTC.
- F7 only the TOP projected contender gated deferral; every in-gap
  contender's game now counts (LockDecision.contender_game_pks).
- F3 a scheduled check overrunning the fallback deadline launched a SECOND
  full cascade; its fresh LockDecision is now reused (the floor budgets one).
- F4 the pre/post confirmation syncs fetched the whole slate (worst case
  ~minute/game in retries, twice); bounded to the remaining runs' games and
  skipped on the reuse path.
- F5 an undelivered preview whose game started classified as locked and
  stranded the day; it is archived (stale_pick_*) and re-selected.
- F6 delivery_refusals + fallback_refreshes now survive same-day restarts.
- F9 measured durations merged chronologically (reused entries excluded).
- F1 (partial) pre-send cutoff re-check at the last responsible moment;
  residual race = the transport's own seconds, documented.
- F2 (partial) the crash-idempotency locked_unconfirmed branch now pages
  CRITICAL; the delivery_unknown/non-scoreable redesign is a recorded
  follow-up (streak-scoring semantics out of scope).
- F11 the late_delivery WARN threshold tracks the configured reserve.
- F13 doc corrections (undelivered days do NOT surface via late_delivery;
  ~5-min cascades labeled as expected-pending-verification).

Deferred with reasons in the audit doc: F2 full redesign, F10 feed-file
validation, F1 in-transport deadline. Disagreed: splitting the pair-
correlation audit off the branch (docs-only, zero runtime surface).

commits.subject: fix(scheduler): rebase reconciliation — commit immutability beats past-cutoff archive
commits.body:
The branch was built on a base predating the 2026-08-14 silent-pass fixes
(Warmup classification, committed-means-immutable, delivery_attempted
durable marker). The rebase auto-merged with no textual conflicts but the
wrong ORDER in run_single_check: the past-cutoff archive (Codex r2 F5) ran
before the scoreable-decision check, so a same-day restart could archive a
private_locked commit or erase the delivery_attempted crash marker.

Reordered: scoreable decision on disk wins first; the archive additionally
refuses to touch a delivery_attempted pick. Both pinned with tests.

commits.subject: feat(health): late_delivery source; fallback_defer compares both slots
commits.body:
late_delivery is the EOD backstop for the delivery-cutoff guard: CRITICAL
when the day's pick was sent at/after first pitch − 5 (DailyPick.delivered_at,
falling back to scheduler_state.pick_locked_at) or when the scheduler
refused a late delivery; WARN inside the operator reserve. fallback_defer's
never-miss check only asked whether a delivered pick file exists — which is
exactly how the 13:36 DM for a 13:35 cutoff read as healthy — and its
same_pick now also compares the double-down (Codex review #10).
